property_summary: When sendTo is called from any caller and does not revert, the transfer amount can be greater than 1 ether (i.e., there is no enforced 1 ether upper cap).

For any caller who is the owner and any nonzero receiver/address and positive amount, the reference contract C allows transferring any positive amount (no upper bound) whereas the mutant rejects (reverts) when amount > 1 ether; thus for some fuzzed amount > 1 ether the mutant will fail while the reference succeeds.

For any caller who is the owner, any non-zero receiver address, and any positive amount, the reference contract always succeeds in transferring that amount (call returns/does not revert), while the mutant will revert for some inputs where amount > 1 ether, so the property is: for admissible inputs the call to sendTo MUST not revert (reference holds for all admissible inputs we allow), and the mutant violates this for amounts above 1 ether.

For any caller who is the contract owner, any non-zero receiver address that is a contract that accepts arbitrary-sized Ether transfers, and any positive amount, calling sendTo should succeed (not revert) on the reference; the mutant that caps transfers to 1 ether will revert for some fuzzed amounts > 1 ether, so the property is that sendTo does not revert for all admissible inputs while the mutant violates this.
